title: WPMS/1525/2022 of SATYAVEER SAINI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1525 of 2022
Satyaveer Saini ... Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Others ... Respondents
Advocates : Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, Advocate, for the petitioner
Mr. V.D. Bisen, Brief Holder, for the State
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
With the consent of the parties, the writ petition is being
taken up for its final consideration, because looking to the
delicacy of dispute, which is involved consideration in the
present writ petition, and the facts and circumstances, which
have been narrated therein, the writ petition itself could be
decided, based on the consensus, which has been extended by
the respondent's counsel, that the issue stands covered by the
judgements, rendered by this Court (i) in Writ Petition (M/S) No.
3710 of 2018, as decided on 11th March 2019; (ii) in Writ
Petition (M/S) No. 107 of 2021, as decided on 6th August 2021;
and (iii) in Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2202 of 2020, as decided on
24th August 2021. The parity of the judgements as claimed by
the petitioner, is a fact which is not disputed by the counsel for
the respondent.
2. But, still, looking to the facts and circumstances under
which the petitioner has modulated his reliefs, questioning the
propriety of the impugned orders dated 4th February 2022, and
8
th May 2022, as it has been passed by respondent No. 3,
whereby the petitioner's application, for the grant of caste
certificate, i.e. for the OBC (Saini) caste, to which the petitioner

2
belongs, the same has been rejected and that too without
assigning any reasons for rejection.

3. The petitioner has come up with the case, that he is a
permanent resident of the State of Uttarakhand, and reckoning
the aforesaid facts, that he happens to be a permanent resident
of the State of Uttarakhand, the competent authority had issued
him with a permanent resident certificate, as back as on 7th
December 2016, fortifying the fact, that the petitioner is a
permanent resident of village Bahbalpur Hansowala, Tehsil
Bhagwanpur, District Haridwar.
4. It's not even that, after the issuance of the said certificate,
which was issued to the petitioner on 7th December 2016, there
is yet another permanent resident certificate, which had been
issued by the respondents competent authority on 19th
February 2022, fortifying and reiterating the aforesaid fact, that
the petitioner is a permanent resident of the State of
Uttarakhand. It's not even that, even after reckoning of the
petitioner, to be a permanent resident of the State of
Uttarakhand, he was also issued with a caste certificate as back
as on 11th January 2017, by the competent authority, based on
the report, which was submitted by the Patwari Lekhpal on 11th
January 2017. Hence, the petitioner contends, that he would be
entitled to be issued with the caste certificate in the terms of the
Government Orders, which he has referred to in the present writ
petition, coupled with the fact, that after the issuance of the
aforesaid permanent resident certificates and caste certificate,
in fact, no controversy as such, remains to be resolved as of

3
now, which could have mandated the petitioner to place
evidence on record, to show his length of residence in the State
of Uttarakhand.
5. Apparently, this Court is of the view, that in fact,
respondent No. 3, has maliciously rejected the application of the
petitioner, despite that though their own officers have earlier
issued the permanent resident certificate, as well as the caste
certificate to the petitioner which still holds to be good.
6. The impugned order, apart from the fact that it was
passed without any reasoning, it apparently smacks malice.
Once the petitioner was born in the State of Uttarakhand, he
had acquired the qualification within the territorial domain of
the State, and he has been reckoned as to be a permanent
resident of the State, when his caste has been recognised by the
Competent State Authority, and that too, based upon the report,
which was solicited by them, this Court finds no logic, or valid
reason as to how and why the responded No. 3, could have still
rejected the application of the petitioner for issuance of the
caste certificate.
7. In that eventuality, while allowing the writ petition, and
setting aside impugned orders dated 4th February 2022 and 8th
May 2022, a writ of mandamus is issued to respondent No. 3, to
issue an OBC caste certificate to the petitioner of being a person
belonging to the "Saini" caste. The necessary caste certificate
would be issued within a period of four weeks from today.

4
8. But, the manner in which the respondent No. 3, has
proceeded to reject the application of the petitioner, this Court
is of a confirmed opinion, that owing to the official document,
which are on record, which fall to be within the definition of
being a public document, I don't see any logic in the act of
respondent No. 3, in rejecting the application of the petitioner
for issuing caste certificate, and consequentially forcing litigation
on him, and that too, without assigning any reason, and it rather
smacks malice on part of respondent No. 3, hence, the District
Magistrate, district Haridwar, is directed to take an appropriate
disciplinary action, against responded No. 3, for acting in a
manner unlike a public officer.
9. Subject to the aforesaid, the writ petition stands allowed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
01.07.2022
Mahinder/
